purpose: Shift the surviving Japanese Marshall submarine information/intercept network from fast-carrier tracking toward the assault/support echelons and resolve attacks without converting Branch liaison into a magic hit bonus.

notes: One SenTaka contact boat from 2-Feb is mission-damaged and leaves same-day shadow duty but survives.
Indian-Ocean seven-boat layer remains separate and unchanged.
Boats are redistributed toward transport, CVE/fire-support and logistics corridors once Japanese carriers break contact.

US_ASW_context: high readiness after repeated submarine reports and GALVANIC experience

events.event: HQ uses carrier-contact tracks, transport reports and landing timetable inference to shift outer/middle boats toward Kwajalein approaches; several contacts are escorts/auxiliaries only.
events.result: No credited weapon hit; reporting narrows the main assault corridors and confirms that the amphibious force continues despite the 3-Feb carrier exchange.

events.event: One northern-sector boat approaches a CVE/fire-support screen but is forced deep by air/escort search before a satisfactory shot.
events.result: No launch centered; preserves boat rather than firing a very low-quality long-range spread.

events.event: A middle-layer conventional I/Ro-class boat gets a firing solution on the southern tractor/transport echelon. Six-torpedo-class spread centered against the transport mass.
events.centered_hit: One torpedo hits LST-224, one of the historical Southern Tractor Unit LSTs. Severe flooding/fire; constructive total loss/sinks after abandonment centered.
events.personnel_and_cargo_effect: About 70-110 total killed/missing/wounded centered ~90 plus loss of embarked vehicles/stores; exact unit cargo not invented. Assault craft/vehicle allocations are redistributed across surviving LST/LCI/APA lift.
events.operational_effect: Southern assault organization loses roughly one of eight tractor-unit LST hulls; local boat/vehicle density and unloading margin fall, but the division-scale landing is not stopped.

events.event: US escorts counterattack the firing sector. The attacker uses disciplined withdrawal and acoustic-deception procedures but receives depth-charge shock/leaks.
events.result: Attacker survives centered but becomes MISSION_DAMAGED_WITHDRAW, not available for another pre-D-Day attack.

events.event: A separate middle/inner Japanese boat attempts to penetrate the northern/central screen. Radar/sonar handoff followed by depth-charge/Hedgehog prosecution produces a centered submarine loss.
events.result: One Japanese conventional submarine sunk centered; exact historical hull identity deliberately not forced because 1944 Marshall submarine-loss attributions are disputed and Branch patrol geometry differs.

events.event: Remaining boats report transport concentration and fire-support movement but heavy ASW prevents another weapon-quality shot before the main landings.

net_result_through_6Feb.US_ships: LST-224 constructive total loss centered; no APA/CVE/battleship hit centered.
net_result_through_6Feb.Japan_submarines: 1 conventional boat sunk centered; 2 boats mission-damaged/withdrawn including the prior SenTaka contact boat; remaining local network still reports but is increasingly pushed outward.
net_result_through_6Feb.information_effect: Japanese command receives reliable confirmation of landing timing/sector concentration; this improves local readiness but cannot compensate for suppressed airfields and overwhelming naval gunfire.
net_result_through_6Feb.anti_double_count: Do not separately add a generic submarine hit/survival bonus. The LST hit is the realized payoff of the same contact/fusion system already modeled.
